capitals.name: Colombo
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Colombo'; the Kandyan kings' capital was Kandy until 1815.

correction.text: the coastal provinces taken from the Dutch in 1796, with the Jaffna peninsula

keyframe_review.note: 1796-1813, 28,908 km2 (bbox 79.9-81.7 E, 6.6-8.8 N): the coastal belt taken from the Dutch, about 0.44 of the 65,993 km2 the British Ceylon infobox gives for 1946, the rest being the Kingdom of Kandy until 1815 ('Much of the Kandy Kingdom's territory was in Sri Lanka's mountainous and thickly forested interior'; the Dutch had been given 'all of Kandy's coastal provinces' in 1765). The Kandy page has the British taking 'the entirety of Jaffna' with Batticaloa and the coast; the outline stops at 8.8 N and leaves the Jaffna peninsula out, so it is added. Colombo fell in February 1796 (infobox of British Ceylon: 'Capture of Dutch Ceylon: 5 March 1796').

1814, 28,908 km2, the same coastal belt as 1796-1813; the Kandyan Convention of 2 March 1815 (infobox 'Signing of Kandyan Convention: 2 March 1815') follows in the next year. Jaffna is the same addition as in the 1796 verdict.

correction.text: the whole island of Ceylon: Dutch coast, the former Kingdom of Kandy and the northern Vanni

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1815-1947: after 'In 1815 Kandy was captured in the Second Kandyan War, ending Sri Lankan independence' the colony is the whole island. Cliopatria has no British Ceylon shape after 1814: the British Empire row (to 1858) and the British Raj row (1859-1946) both carry all of Sri Lanka, the Raj wrongly (Ceylon was 'a jurisdiction distinct from India', the page says), and the Sri Lanka row starts only in 1948. The island is 65,993 km2 by the 1946 infobox and 60,443 km2 by the gazetteer's cell count (ratio 0.92). The Kandy page says the kingdom 'definitively lost its autonomy following the Uva Rebellion of 1817'; the British Ceylon page says the British 'annexed the Kingdom of Kandy to British Ceylon in 1817'.

region.text: the coastal provinces of the Dutch: the south-west, west and east coasts and Jaffna

ledger.note: 1796: the British take Dutch Ceylon. Colombo falls in February ('by the 15 of that month, Colombo had fallen and Dutch rule on the island had come to an end'; the dutch-ceylon dossier has 14 February 1796); the British Ceylon infobox says 'Capture of Dutch Ceylon: 5 March 1796' and has the island first a 'Chartered territory of East India Company under India (1795/96-1802)'. The Kandy page has Batticaloa taken on 18 September and 'the entirety of Jaffna' on 28 September, year not on the sentence.

1802: Ceylon becomes a Crown colony. 'Proclamation of the Crown colony: 25 March 1802' (infobox); the Kandy page has the coast 'formally ceded to the British under the Treaty of Amiens in 1802'. The colony and its dossier continue.

region.text: the Kingdom of Kandy, the mountainous interior

ledger.note: 1803: the First Kandyan War. 'On 31 January 1803, a British force led by General Hay Macdowall marched to Kandy and found it evacuated'; the British Ceylon page says the Kandyan refusal 'led eventually (1803) to the 1st Kandyan War, but was repulsed'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Kandy, the mountainous interior

ledger.note: 1805: the war ends in a truce. 'an uneasy truce was in place by 1805' (Kandy page); no treaty or day is given and no ground changed hands.

region.text: the Kingdom of Kandy, the mountainous interior

ledger.note: 1815: the Second Kandyan War. 'Kandy was seized on 14 February, and Sri Wickrama Rajasinghe himself captured on 18 February' (Kandy page; the year follows from the Convention of 2 March 1815 in the next sentences).

region.text: the Kingdom of Kandy: the interior of the island not held by the British in 1814

ledger.note: 1815: the Kingdom of Kandy passes to Britain. 'In 1815 Kandy was captured in the Second Kandyan War, ending Sri Lankan independence'; 'Signing of Kandyan Convention: 2 March 1815' (infobox; the Kandy page: 'On 2 March 1815, British agents - including Robert Brownrigg and John D'Oyly - met with the nobility'). The British Ceylon page also says the British 'annexed the Kingdom of Kandy to British Ceylon in 1817', after the Uva Rebellion (1817-1818).

region.text: the Kingdom of Kandy, the mountainous interior

ledger.note: 1815: the war ends with the Kandyan Convention of 2 March 1815; the Uva Rebellion that began in 1817 is the 'Third Kandyan War' of the page.

region.text: the whole island, which becomes the Dominion of Ceylon

ledger.note: 1948: independence. 'Independence: 4 February 1948' (infobox); the Soulbury constitution led to the Dominion of Ceylon; 'between 1796 and 4 February 1948' the island was a British Crown colony.

wars.name: First Kandyan War
wars.outcome: The British force 'marched to Kandy and found it evacuated' on 31 January 1803 and the attempt 'was repulsed'; 'an uneasy truce was in place by 1805'. No ground changed hands.
wars.note: The British Ceylon page: 'led eventually (1803) to the 1st Kandyan War, but was repulsed'.

wars.name: Second Kandyan War
wars.outcome: Kandy seized on 14 February 1815 and the king captured on 18 February; the Kandyan Convention of 2 March 1815 ended the kingdom's independence.
wars.note: The Kandy page does not use the name 'Second Kandyan War'; the British Ceylon page does.

wars.name: Uva Rebellion

zones.text: the Uva duchy and the interior

wars.outcome: The rising 'commencing in the duchy of Uva in 1817' (also called the Third Kandyan War) was put down; the Kandyan leaders were beheaded on 26 November 1817 and the kingdom 'definitively lost its autonomy'.
wars.note: The page gives no end date; the Kandy page has the kingdom under British colonial rule by 1818.

certainty.note: The frontier with the Kingdom of Kandy was a line of forts and passes, not a surveyed boundary.
An island: the coast is the border.

notes: Written by sa-06-d from two pages (budget 1-2). ONE STATE OR TWO: Cliopatria's 'Ceylon' (1236-1506, the Sinhalese kingdoms; dossier ceylon) and 'British Ceylon' (1796-1814) share Wikidata Q918153, but they are different states four centuries apart; the id is the island's article, not an identity. This dossier covers British Ceylon only and extends it from Cliopatria's 1796-1814 to the colony's real life 1796-1948 with a new keyframe for 1815-1947. CLIOPATRIA ROW: the 1796-1814 outline is the coastal belt without the Jaffna peninsula (corrected in the 1796 verdict); after 1814 the island is drawn inside the British Empire row and, wrongly, inside the British Raj row (the british-raj dossier subtracts it); the Sri Lanka row starts in 1948. NOT RESOLVED: the exact day of the Dutch surrender (14 or 15 February 1796 on the Kandy and dutch-ceylon pages against 5 March 1796 in the British Ceylon infobox; the Kandy page's September dates for Batticaloa and Jaffna lack the year and the page also writes 1795 for Jaffna); the Vanni chieftaincies (listed as a predecessor in the infobox, with no date); the 1802 Treaty of Amiens (named on the Kandy page, not the British Ceylon page); the Matale rebellion of 1848 and the Donoughmore and Soulbury constitutions (no territory); the governors (the infobox gives only Frederick North 1798-1805 and Sir Henry Monck-Mason Moore 1944-1948, so no ruler strip); the Ceylon Independence Act (not named on the page). COUNTERPARTS: dutch-ceylon, kingdom-of-kandy and sri-lanka have dossiers (kingdom-of-kandy ends 2 March 1815 with british-ceylon as successor). 'Kandyan rebels (Uva)' needs no dossier.
